use.reason: The actual E_l is a nonsingular elliptic curve over Q with conductor N; the theorem's explicit curve quantifier applies. Take the theorem's associated form, with its stated integral Fourier coefficients and trivial nebentypus. The trace comparison ranges over q not dividing 2N. Shimura needs eigenform status at all operators, not trace comparison at all primes. The p.1007 normalized convention and the p.1010 Euler series with constant term one identify the association's a_1=1. No rescaling is inferred from prime traces. The same f, level N, and integer coefficients enter both subsequent cards. Normalized Fourier T_q gives a_q as eigenvalue by its n=1 coefficient. At level primes use the U_p coefficient rule, not a good-prime Euler factor. Good trace comparison uses the actual reductions of E_l. Since v_2(Delta)=8 for odd l and model change alters it by multiples of 12, 2 divides N for this curve. No equality at excluded primes is extracted. The theorem-heading attribution does not change the stated hypothesis. Shimura gets a common normalized eigenform with coefficient field Q; Faltings gets the stated comparison only outside a finite set.

use.reason: Use Gamma=Gamma0(N) and the normalized simultaneous eigenfunction; the level group lies in the required range. The quotient is over Q and has dimension [Q:Q]=1. The unital Q-coefficient action is integer multiplication on integral scalars. Shimura's eigenrelation includes all its T_n. This card consumes its good-prime relation and its almost-all Euler comparison. Pulling back differentials along z to qz and (z+j)/q gives exactly q f(qz)+q^-1 sum_j f((z+j)/q). Moduli cyclic quotients and their duals exchange the two projections for q coprime to N. Use the same J0(N) and q_f on the degree-zero divisor classes, not a polarisation-dual map or a tangent-space substitute. No degree or averaging factor is inserted. A rationalized morphism equality descends to integral Hom by torsion-freeness. The good correspondence has q+1 branches at infinity, all fixing it. The rational cusp gives the Pic0 map and no extra constant. The Gamma0(N) branch makes the alternative Fricke condition unnecessary. No bad Euler, Atkin–Lehner, integral lattice or model extension conclusion is claimed. Postcompose with alpha and apply to [x]-[infinity]. The unaveraged CM and reduced neighbor relations consume this operator with their separate CM and reduction inputs.
